questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Opportunities in Santa Barbara as the 5th best public university in the US. Their TMP (Technology Management Program) especially caught my interest, and as exchange students we have full access to this Business oriented department which is very rare.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Decently easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not really any

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Not easy at all. There is basically a housing crisis and as an exchange student you are in a ver vulnarable position. Expect to pay 1000-2000 USD per month in rent.
We found housing by contacting all real estate and renting agencies in the area, and were lucky to find a newly renovated unit that was vacant and that we could rent for only 6 months. Usuallt contracts are written for 12 months, which is unfornunate for 2 quarter exchange students.
Housing through the university or using facebook housing groups to find a bed in a shared room is what most people do, so you end up living 2-5 people in one room together.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living is Isla Vista is really nice, fun people, fun parties and close to campus, but it is damn expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
There should be made better housing opportunities available for exchange students, given how exchange students are in a very weak position. Normally, leases are written 6-8 months on advance, which is impossible for exchange students because of the visa process.
Offering 2000 USD per month housing for exchange students is not viable.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Most is online. The main thing is you order an access card online that you have to pick up at campus. It is quite easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email to counselors

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very, but it was hard sometimes. Make sure to get pre approval from host university to take courses good time in advance.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get approved for courses weeks before the enrollment pass opens up.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: TMP courses were great. PSTAT courses were also quite nice. ECON courses were not very engaging or good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very different structure than at UCPH. Lots of obligatory stuff. But in general it is easier to do well than it is at UCPH. You more or less just have to show up and turn in mandatory stuff to do well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: TMP and PSTAT courses were much more interactive and professors really care. A much closer connection with the lecturer. ECON courses were big lectures were you just sat and listenede for 90 minutes and then went on your way.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON 135 Monetary Economics
ECON 181 International Finance
TMP 122 Entrepreneurship
TMP 127 Managing Technology Organizations
TMP 240 Business Strategy & Leadership 
PSTAT 194FM Financial Market Risk & Modeling

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
TMP 122 Entrepreneurship
TMP 127 Managing Technology Organizations
TMP 240 Business Strategy & Leadership 
PSTAT 194FM Financial Market Risk & Modeling

They were all great courses that you cannot get at UCPH.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Free gym. Cheap excursion club with lots of tours and free surf boards.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel, becuase california is awesome!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel! And go to some crazy isla ista parties!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. At UCSB people are very welcoming and nice. Also, exchange students are much more normal in the US, so people are more accostumed to accommodate them.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go up and say hi.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No being allowed to drink in public, and all the civil restrictions in general.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The "hiking" mindset of so many people. Everyone goes in hikes all the time and it is great!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Start looking for housing early, and write all rental agencies to see if they have any vacancies where you can do a 6 month rental.
Take TMP courses, as you get so many more friends in those courses and learn much more.
Go out and travel.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready to pay a lot in rent and share a room with 2-3-4 strangers.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many inspiring people and travelling to see so much amazing nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All the bureaucracy

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
